title: टेकुमा फोहोरबाट ऊर्जा उत्पादन परीक्षण सुरू
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले टेकुको फोहोरबाट ऊर्जा उत्पादन परियोजनाको परीक्षण सुरु गरेको छ । बिहीबार टेकु फोहर संकलन केन्द्रमा ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा सिँचाइमन्त्री विराजभक्त श्रेष्ठ र काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाकी कार्यवाहक प्रमुख सुनिता डंगोलले संयुक्त रुपमा पुनःनिर्मित टेकु बायो–मिथेनेसन प्लान्टको उद्घाटन गरेका हुन् । परियोजनाको परीक्षण सुरु भएसंगै कुहिने फोहोरको व्यवस्थापनका साथै नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा र जैविक मल उत्पादनसँग जोड्ने नीति अघि बढाउने सहज हुने महानगरको विश्वास छ । कार्यक्रममा ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत तथा सिँचाइमन्त्री श्रेष्ठले ७५३ वटै स्थानीय पालिकालाई यस्ता कार्यक्रम सुरु गर्न आह्वान गर्दै समन्वय भएमा त्यस्तै प्लान्टमा साझेदार बन्न मन्त्रालय तयार रहेको बताए । ’एलपीजी मुक्त स्थानीय सरकार’ घोषणाअनुसार उत्पादन हुने ग्यासलाई उपयोग गर्न नीतिगत अस्पष्टतामा सहकार्य गर्नुपर्ने उनले बताए । उनले नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा तथा ऊर्जा दक्षता विधेयक संसद्मा दर्ता भइसकेको सन्दर्भमा पाइपलाइन र ग्यास वितरणसम्बन्धी विषयमा संसद्मा घनिभूत छलफल गरी नीतिगत सम्बोधन वा छुट्टै प्रावधान आवश्यक पर्ने–नपर्नेबारे छलफल गर्न सकिने धारणा राखे । उनले फोहर व्यवस्थापनमा सरकारी तथा जिम्मेवार निकाय मात्र सक्रिय भएर नपुग्ने भएकाले आम नागरिकमा जनचेतना अभिवृद्धि र सहयोग अपरिहार्य रहेको धारणा राखे । त्यस्तै काठमाडौं महानगरकी कार्यवाहक प्रमुख डंगोलले बायोग्यास प्लान्ट सञ्चालनपछि उत्पादन हुने ग्यास कसरी वितरण गर्ने भन्ने स्पष्ट नीति अझै नबनेको, घर–घरमा सिलिन्डर पु¥याउने पाटोसँगै पाइपलाइन वितरणको नीति तत्काल आवश्यक रहेको बताइन् । परीक्षण सञ्चालन सुरु भई ग्यास उत्पादन हुन थालेपछि वितरणको अन्योल हुने भएकाले पाइपलाइन वितरणसम्बन्धी नीति छिटो ल्याउन उहाले आग्रह गरिन् । उनले फोहोरलाई मोहर बनाउने, ’वेस्ट टु इनर्जी’ तथा ’वेस्ट टु इकोनोमी’ का विविध पक्षलाई समेट्दै फोहोरको उपयोगी प्रयोग गर्न छुट्टै नीति आवश्यक रहेको धारणा राखिन् । करिव १० बर्ष अघि निर्र्माण भएको टेकु बायो–मिथेनेसन प्लान्ट केहि समयमा नै बन्द भएको थियो । महानगरले वैकल्पिक ऊर्जा प्रवद्र्धन केन्द्रसंगको समन्वयमा पुनः परिक्षण सुरु गरेको हो । Kathmandu. Kathmandu Metropolitan City has started testing a waste-to-energy project in Teku. Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Acting Mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City Sunita Dangol jointly inaugurated the reconstructed Teku Bio-Methanation Plant at the Teku Waste Collection Center on Thursday. The metropolis believes that once the project testing begins, it will be easier to move forward with policies linking the management of biodegradable waste with renewable energy and organic fertilizer production. At the event, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Shrestha called on all 753 local municipalities to start such programs and said that the ministry is ready to become a partner in such plants if there is coordination. He said that cooperation is needed in the policy ambiguity to utilize the gas produced as per the declaration of 'LPG-free local government'. He opined that in the context of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill having been registered in the Parliament, the issues related to pipeline and gas distribution can be discussed in depth in the Parliament and whether a policy-level address or separate provisions are required. He opined that increasing public awareness and cooperation among the general public is indispensable as only the government and responsible bodies are active in waste management. Similarly, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, Dangol, said that a clear policy on how to distribute the gas produced after the biogas plant is operational has not yet been formulated, and a policy on pipeline distribution is urgently needed along with the provision of cylinders to every household. She urged that a policy on pipeline distribution be brought soon as there will be confusion over distribution once the trial operation begins and gas production begins. She opined that a separate policy is needed for the beneficial use of waste, covering various aspects of waste-to-energy, waste-to-economy, and waste-to-sealing. The Teku Bio-Methanation Plant, which was built about 10 years ago, was closed for some time. The metropolis has started testing again in coordination with the Alternative Energy Promotion Center.

Kathmandu Metropolitan City has started testing a waste-to-energy project in Teku. Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Acting Mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City Sunita Dangol jointly inaugurated the reconstructed Teku Bio-Methanation Plant at the Teku Waste Collection Center on Thursday. The metropolis believes that once the project testing begins, it will be easier to move forward with policies linking the management of biodegradable waste with renewable energy and organic fertilizer production. At the event, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Shrestha called on all 753 local municipalities to start such programs and said that the ministry is ready to become a partner in such plants if there is coordination. He said that cooperation is needed in the policy ambiguity to utilize the gas produced as per the declaration of 'LPG-free local government'. He opined that in the context of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill having been registered in the Parliament, the issues related to pipeline and gas distribution can be discussed in depth in the Parliament and whether a policy-level address or separate provisions are required. He opined that increasing public awareness and cooperation among the general public is indispensable as only the government and responsible bodies are active in waste management. Similarly, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, Dangol, said that a clear policy on how to distribute the gas produced after the biogas plant is operational has not yet been formulated, and a policy on pipeline distribution is urgently needed along with the provision of cylinders to every household. She urged that a policy on pipeline distribution be brought soon as there will be confusion over distribution once the trial operation begins and gas production begins. She opined that a separate policy is needed for the beneficial use of waste, covering various aspects of waste-to-energy, waste-to-economy, and waste-to-sealing. The Teku Bio-Methanation Plant, which was built about 10 years ago, was closed for some time. The metropolis has started testing again in coordination with the Alternative Energy Promotion Center.

त्यस्तै काठमाडौं महानगरकी कार्यवाहक प्रमुख डंगोलले बायोग्यास प्लान्ट सञ्चालनपछि उत्पादन हुने ग्यास कसरी वितरण गर्ने भन्ने स्पष्ट नीति अझै नबनेको, घर–घरमा सिलिन्डर पु¥याउने पाटोसँगै पाइपलाइन वितरणको नीति तत्काल आवश्यक रहेको बताइन् । परीक्षण सञ्चालन सुरु भई ग्यास उत्पादन हुन थालेपछि वितरणको अन्योल हुने भएकाले पाइपलाइन वितरणसम्बन्धी नीति छिटो ल्याउन उहाले आग्रह गरिन् ।

उनले फोहोरलाई मोहर बनाउने, ’वेस्ट टु इनर्जी’ तथा ’वेस्ट टु इकोनोमी’ का विविध पक्षलाई समेट्दै फोहोरको उपयोगी प्रयोग गर्न छुट्टै नीति आवश्यक रहेको धारणा राखिन् । करिव १० बर्ष अघि निर्र्माण भएको टेकु बायो–मिथेनेसन प्लान्ट केहि समयमा नै बन्द भएको थियो । महानगरले वैकल्पिक ऊर्जा प्रवद्र्धन केन्द्रसंगको समन्वयमा पुनः परिक्षण सुरु गरेको हो ।

Kathmandu. Kathmandu Metropolitan City has started testing a waste-to-energy project in Teku. Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Acting Mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City Sunita Dangol jointly inaugurated the reconstructed Teku Bio-Methanation Plant at the Teku Waste Collection Center on Thursday. The metropolis believes that once the project testing begins, it will be easier to move forward with policies linking the management of biodegradable waste with renewable energy and organic fertilizer production. At the event, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Shrestha called on all 753 local municipalities to start such programs and said that the ministry is ready to become a partner in such plants if there is coordination. He said that cooperation is needed in the policy ambiguity to utilize the gas produced as per the declaration of 'LPG-free local government'. He opined that in the context of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill having been registered in the Parliament, the issues related to pipeline and gas distribution can be discussed in depth in the Parliament and whether a policy-level address or separate provisions are required. He opined that increasing public awareness and cooperation among the general public is indispensable as only the government and responsible bodies are active in waste management. Similarly, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, Dangol, said that a clear policy on how to distribute the gas produced after the biogas plant is operational has not yet been formulated, and a policy on pipeline distribution is urgently needed along with the provision of cylinders to every household. She urged that a policy on pipeline distribution be brought soon as there will be confusion over distribution once the trial operation begins and gas production begins. She opined that a separate policy is needed for the beneficial use of waste, covering various aspects of waste-to-energy, waste-to-economy, and waste-to-sealing. The Teku Bio-Methanation Plant, which was built about 10 years ago, was closed for some time. The metropolis has started testing again in coordination with the Alternative Energy Promotion Center.
